title: `@tool` resources share the same `Array`/`Packed_Array` references upon "Paste as Unique"/"Make Unique" duplications, causing unwanted mutations.
body:
### Tested versions

Godot v4.7.2.stable (ed1daf0bf)

### System information

Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21043.19003) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.94 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

The title is pretty self-explanatory, but to reiterate, when duplicating a `@tool` resource in the editor, one would expect arrays to not be shared when making the resource "Unique". This is not the case, leading to frustrating results.

I believe this has gone largely unnoticed due to how `@export` just overwrites the array with a new one when modified in the inspector. However, my specific use-case has an internal array put under `@export_storage`, with four accessor variables that manipulate it.

Example:
```gdscript
@export_group("Corners")
## Position of the upper-left corner.
@export_custom(PROPERTY_HINT_NONE, "", PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR)
var up_left := Vector2.ZERO:   get = get_up_left,    set = set_up_left

## Position of the upper-right corner.
@export_custom(PROPERTY_HINT_NONE, "", PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR)
var up_right := Vector2.RIGHT: get = get_up_right,   set = set_up_right

## Position of the lower-right corner.
@export_custom(PROPERTY_HINT_NONE, "", PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR)
var down_right := Vector2.ONE: get = get_down_right, set = set_down_right

## Position of the lower-left corner.
@export_custom(PROPERTY_HINT_NONE, "", PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR)
var down_left := Vector2.DOWN: get = get_down_left,  set = set_down_left

@export_storage
var _corners: PackedVector2Array = [Vector2.ZERO, Vector2.RIGHT, Vector2.ONE, Vector2.DOWN]
```

```gdscript
func get_up_left()    -> Vector2: return _corners[Corner.CORNER_TOP_LEFT]
func get_up_right()   -> Vector2: return _corners[Corner.CORNER_TOP_RIGHT]
func get_down_right() -> Vector2: return _corners[Corner.CORNER_BOTTOM_RIGHT]
func get_down_left()  -> Vector2: return _corners[Corner.CORNER_BOTTOM_LEFT]

func set_up_left(value: Vector2) -> void:
	_corners[Corner.CORNER_TOP_LEFT]     = value; _mark_dirty()
func set_up_right(value: Vector2) -> void:
	_corners[Corner.CORNER_TOP_RIGHT]    = value; _mark_dirty()
func set_down_right(value: Vector2) -> void:
	_corners[Corner.CORNER_BOTTOM_RIGHT] = value; _mark_dirty()
func set_down_left(value: Vector2) -> void:
	_corners[Corner.CORNER_BOTTOM_LEFT]  = value; _mark_dirty()
```
While I recognize that this is an unconventional use-case (I _do_ have my reasons), I'd imagine resources designed around custom property list generation to construct a more palatable interface for their internal arrays would _also_ suffer under this specific bug.

Anyway, I believe that this issue is a result of the editor using `Resource.duplicate()`, which returns a shallow copy.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/57277407e77e61b161f35dbd7aeb510f7a9e26a6/editor/inspector/editor_resource_picker.cpp#L499-L508
I don't know if this is the only place this function has been used for resource duplication in the editor code, but it's worth highlighting.

I think that using `duplicate_deep(RESOURCE_DEEP_DUPLICATE_NONE)` in the relevant areas instead would be an acceptable fix, but I can't exactly claim to be familiar enough with the Godot editor's inner workings to know if this fix would be acceptable.

Finding a workaround for this issue is rather difficult, given how GDScript doesn't allow you to overwrite `duplicate()` behavior. One may suggest just simply having arrays duplicate themselves in `_init()`, but the resource duplication code applies the properties _after_ `_init()` is ran, making this approach rather pointless.

In the end, I had to make it so that Godot would automatically duplicate the array whenever it was written to in the editor:
```gdscript
func set_up_left(value: Vector2) -> void:
	_write_corner(Corner.CORNER_TOP_LEFT, value)
func set_up_right(value: Vector2) -> void:
	_write_corner(Corner.CORNER_TOP_RIGHT, value)
func set_down_right(value: Vector2) -> void:
	_write_corner(Corner.CORNER_BOTTOM_RIGHT, value)
func set_down_left(value: Vector2) -> void:
	_write_corner(Corner.CORNER_BOTTOM_LEFT, value)

func _write_corner(corner: Corner, value: Vector2) -> void:
	if Engine.is_editor_hint(): _own_corners()
	_corners[corner] = value
	_mark_dirty()

func _own_corners() -> void:
	_corners = _corners.duplicate()
```
…This isn't exactly ideal, but it functions at least.

### Steps to reproduce

This should be pretty straightforward.

1. Make a `@tool` resource akin to this:
```gdscript
@tool
extends Resource
class_name Vector2ArrayAccessor

@export_custom(PROPERTY_HINT_NONE, "", PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR)
var vec2: Vector2 = Vector2.ZERO:
	set(value): _vec2_internal[0] = value
	get(): return _vec2_internal[0]

@export_storage
var _vec2_internal: PackedVector2Array = [Vector2.ZERO]
```

2. Make a scene with a node that has a script with something like `@export var accessors: Array[Vector2ArrayAccessor] = []` attached to it.
3. Resize the array in the scene to allow two entries. Make a new resource in the first entry, and then make a "Unique" duplicate for it in the second entry. Modify the second resources's accessor property, and then go back to examine the first resource.

Assuming this all was set up correctly, the first resource's accessor property should now be visibly mutated.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

This MRP follows all the above steps except for the last one. Follow the last step yourself, and you should see the expected results.

[resource-array-duplication-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32426778/resource-array-duplication-bug.zip)
